title: Recommendation strength review: Hazira gas terminal release and fire, 2020
audience: Function managers, the people designing corrective actions, and HSE leads
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document; draft: the investigation status is in progress

incident.title: Hazira gas terminal condensate release and fire

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the ProbeMatrix investigation status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person. Validate before adoption.
The bands, flags, loop counts and spread are the engine's (rec-review); the directions are the analyst's, drawn from the register learnings and their cited findings.

bottom_line.text: The register carries 44 recommendations across 25 learnings: 24 stronger, 15 intermediate and 5 weaker. No learning is flagged as a weak fix for a deep cause.
Each of the 5 weaker changes, training or a procedure, sits beside a stronger or intermediate change in the same learning (LR-02, LR-06, LR-07, LR-08 and LR-12).

Six learnings have nothing stronger than an intermediate change. LR-08 and LR-12 say why and point to the engineering change in LR-09 and LR-10; the directions suggest a stronger change for LR-18, LR-19 and LR-24, and a double-loop one for LR-20.
None of the 44 changes is double-loop, although the register marks 12 learnings double-loop; four directions question the norm or design basis behind LR-05, LR-10, LR-17 and LR-20.

The 9M analysis adds one recommendation for each of the nine Ms, all at the elimination tier. Plant leadership is an audience of the learnings behind 21 of the register's 44 recommendations, more than any other role.

items.text: This review covers the learnings register and the 9M analysis. The strength table bands the register's 44 recommendations across its 25 learnings; the spread table counts the 9M analysis's 9 recommendations, one for each M. The 9M answers come from a scripted replay: they were chosen for demonstration, not by the organisation, so the 9M recommendations show the method rather than the organisation's choices, and all nine sit at the elimination tier because the replay chose it. The 9M analysis's learnings are tied to the register's LR ids through nine-m-map.json.

sections.heading: Strength of change for each learning

items.text: The engine finds 0 double-loop and 44 single-loop changes: every recommendation in the register fixes a condition, and none names an assumption, norm, design basis, target, incentive or budget to question.

The register marks 12 learnings as double-loop (LR-01, LR-02, LR-05, LR-06, LR-07, LR-08, LR-09, LR-10, LR-11, LR-12, LR-17 and LR-20), yet their changes are single-loop. Left unquestioned: why three seal failures in 22 months were handled as routine repairs (LR-05), why fire and gas detection was designed to display rather than act (LR-10), why measured wall loss stayed without a corrective plan for three years and painting was taken as the fix (LR-17), and why recorded compliance on a generic checklist was taken as assurance (LR-20).

items.change: Make the four-year thickness cycle a condition the maintenance system enforces: an inspection on a pressure-boundary line cannot be moved past its due point without the integrity function's recorded assessment of that line.
items.indicator: Thickness inspections on pressure-boundary lines done within the four-year cycle, as a share of those due

items.change: Take an unverified drawing out of isolation planning: isolation and work-planning screens draw their valve and meter lists from a field-verified, controlled P&ID, and a drawing with no verification record cannot be issued for that use.
items.indicator: Isolation plans for the metering system drawn from a field-verified, controlled P&ID, as a share of all such plans

items.change: Make the drill record unable to close without what the drill showed: the drill report cannot be saved as complete until its detection, notification and isolation times and its observations are entered, and each action it raises opens a tracked item.
items.indicator: Drill records closed with timings and observations entered, as a share of all drills

items.change: Question the assumption the audit programme rests on, that a completed checklist shows a barrier works: each audit samples named safety-critical barriers on the plant and records a reading, test or inspection result for each one.
items.indicator: Audit items on safety-critical barriers backed by a recorded reading, test or inspection result
items.why_not_stronger: Assurance is a management activity: no engineered control replaces looking at the plant. The register's change already moves the audit towards site evidence; this direction questions what the audit counts as proof.

items.change: Question the norm that a repeat repair closes the job: a second failure of the same pressure-boundary item within a year is reviewed as a sign that the design or the part is wrong, and the review asks why the earlier repairs were accepted as enough.
items.indicator: Repeat failures on pressure-boundary items reviewed for design or part fitness, as a share of all repeat failures
items.why_not_stronger: The engineering change, an automatic repeat-failure trigger, is already in the register; this direction questions the rule that let three repairs count as enough.

lint_ok.reason: a double-loop direction that questions the rule behind the cause; the engineering change for this learning is already in the register

items.change: Revisit the design basis that let protective systems inform rather than act: list the site's other detection and alarm functions that only display, and record for each whether an automatic action is needed, and the reason when it stays display-only.
items.indicator: Display-only detection and alarm functions with a recorded decision on automatic action
items.why_not_stronger: The engineering change for the metering and Gas Terminal areas is already in the register; this direction asks the same question of the rest of the site.

lint_ok.reason: a double-loop direction that questions the rule behind the cause; the engineering change for this learning is already in the register

items.change: Question the norm that a measurement or a coat of paint closes an integrity finding: wall loss on a line with no corrosion allowance stays open until a fitness-for-service assessment sets the repair, re-rating or replacement.
items.indicator: Integrity findings with wall loss closed on a fitness-for-service assessment, as a share of all such findings
items.why_not_stronger: The register already recommends fitness-for-service work on the known locations; this direction changes what counts as closing the next finding.

lint_ok.reason: a double-loop direction that questions the rule behind the cause; the engineering change for this learning is already in the register

limits: The review reads the text and tier of each recommendation: it cannot tell whether a change is feasible on this site, what it costs, or whether the role that receives it can carry it out.
No owners, due dates or approvals: the organisation sets them when it agrees the actions.
